title: Shami Breaks Silence on India Absence, Sets Sights on Comeback
excerpt: Marking his 100th first-class match with a Duleep Trophy title, the 36-year-old pacer says his eyes are on the "next level" — as selectors insist they stayed in touch through his England-tour absence.
body:
• Mohammed Shami says his motivation has not dipped despite not playing for India since March 2025, insisting his eyes are set on the "next level" in his career.
  • The 36-year-old marked his 100th first-class appearance by helping East Zone win the Duleep Trophy final at Chennai, taking the key wickets of Ravichandran Smaran and Sheikh Rasheed.
  • Shami has found a mentorship role with East Zone's young squad while doubling down on fitness and workload building after years of injury setbacks.
  • A BCCI official has rebutted Shami's earlier claim that selectors did not communicate with him, saying the panel was desperate for his services in England and repeatedly checked on his fitness.

Mohammed Shami has not played for India since March 2025, but the veteran fast bowler made clear after the Duleep Trophy final on Thursday that he has no intention of winding down. His motivation, he said, remains intact, and his sights are still on the next stage of his career.

"There are plenty of reasons to stay motivated if you look for them. At this level, if you aren't self-motivated, your approach is wrong. No matter what stage you're playing at, your eyes must always be set on the next level," Shami said after East Zone defeated South Zone on first-innings lead at Chennai to lift the Duleep Trophy, NDTV reported.

Context & Background

The final carried personal weight for Shami: it was his 100th first-class match. He took two middle-order wickets — Ravichandran Smaran and Sheikh Rasheed — to rock South Zone in the title clash, helping East Zone bundle out their rivals for 336 and seize a match-defining first-innings lead of 372.

"As far as satisfaction goes, achieving this in my 100th match — and that too in a winning Duleep Trophy final — is special. East Zone has won this after a very long time," he said. "Every single boy put his heart and soul into this campaign to get us here. To achieve this in these conditions, in this heat, is outstanding."

Shami's last Test appearance dates back to the World Test Championship final against Australia at the Oval in 2023. A chronic heel issue suffered during the 2023 ODI World Cup, followed by a string of injuries, kept him away from international cricket for more than a year. His absence from the England tour squad this year and the Asia Cup squad fuelled speculation about selection bias, which the pacer has publicly denied he lets affect him.

Impact & Analysis

Behind the scenes, Shami's version of events and the board's have diverged. The 36-year-old had earlier said the Ajit Agarkar-led selection committee did not communicate with him about his non-selection. But a senior BCCI official told PTI that the selectors "were desperate to get his services in England" — where Jasprit Bumrah could not play more than three Tests — and that multiple members of the selection panel messaged Shami about his fitness and asked him to play at least one India A match against England Lions in Canterbury or Northampton, according to Mint. Shami reportedly asked for more time to build his workload.

That dispute is now being overtaken by performance. Shami has requested the ball in crunch domestic moments — East Zone captain Ishan Kishan said he asked to bowl in both the Duleep Trophy quarterfinal and semifinal — and his sharpness in domestic cricket has stood out at a time when India's Test quicks have struggled, prompting fans to recall him fondly, NDTV noted.

Former India bowling coach Bharat Arun has publicly backed the comeback bid, telling the Indian Express that the selectors should not have ended their association with the bowler. "When someone is performing, age shouldn't be a factor," Arun said, calling Shami's durability "outstanding."

"When you wear that crest on your chest, the level of cricket doesn't matter. If you play for the badge, that hunger will naturally show."

— Mohammed Shami

Shami has also settled into a mentoring role with East Zone's young players. He singled out Vaibhav Sooryavanshi — "the kid in our team is literally as old as my career" — and cautioned against over-coaching youngsters who, with IPL experience, "are already quite mature." Tactical input, he said, is reserved for tight moments: "when the game gets tight and challenging, that's when you step in with tactical inputs and remind them to keep fighting."

Diaspora Angle

Shami's comeback push resonates strongly with the Indian diaspora's cricket fans, from New Jersey club players to Bay Area youth coaches who hold him up as the gold standard of seam bowling discipline. In community leagues across the US, his longevity at 36 — built on reverse swing mastery rather than raw pace — is cited as proof that skill and workload management can outlast the early-retirement script.

What's Next

The immediate question is whether sustained domestic output forces a national recall. With India's fast-bowling stocks under pressure in Test cricket, selectors face a straightforward choice: reward the country's most decorated available quick, or stick with youth. "My job is simply to put in the hard work — the rest is in the hands of the Almighty," Shami said, signing off. His next auditions come in the domestic season ahead, where every spell now doubles as a statement of intent.
